title: Recording from the middle of the studio floor
summary: McRae sets balance by standing among the band instead of the control room, and cues the engineer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And did "Moon Ray" the same thing. Just all head. That's what I'm saying. This is the difference between studio -- musicians and musicians that work in the studio all the time that's recording.
See, if you record a lot, you get an ear to the studio. You don't have to hear the sound bouncing away and coming back to you. You could hear that sound.
You could hear everything. When I record -- I don't go in the studio. I go in the middle of the floor with the band.
If I don't hear out there in the middle of the floor -- listen to the band natural, then he's not gonna get it in there.

Because when I finished recording, he say, "Teddy, we're ready. Everything is fine." Then I know he's getting it in there -- everything is cut and dry what I hear out there in the middle of the floor.
See, when I record I get out on the floor.

I don't sit back in the control room and "Hey, turn this up." I get out there and I rehearse the band. I wanna hear it natural. I wanna hear the instruments just like I'm on a bandstand. Then when I hear it out there, I know -- If it's not out there, it's not gonna be on that track, see. And I work much faster that way than sitting in there and telling the guy, "Well, take that over again so and so, I didn't hear so and so." No, I wanna -- "let's do it right here." Stand right in the middle of -- stomp it off, give them the tempo I want -- let's do it right here. And I hear it, okay. The engineer say, "Okay, we got it now. We got it like we want it." He be in there fixing the dials. He know he got it, you know. Then I go in there and tell him where the piano is coming in, so and so and so, you know.
